artboards.title: Price list — one kind, many sizes
Today — the same answer as text

annotations.text:
WHICH DOCUMENT, AND WHEN

The message decides, not the owner.

No quantity asked -> PRICE LIST. Nothing is totalled, because nothing was ordered. This is most of what the matcher now reads: "do you have pull handles", "bolts 6*80, 6*30, 6*60".

A quantity asked -> QUOTATION, the document the app already draws. QTY x RATE = AMOUNT, and a TOTAL.

Forcing a price enquiry into the quotation would invent a quantity of one and a total the customer never asked for.

THE READABILITY WIN IS GROUPING

Five handles become one product name and four short lines, instead of five long ones that repeat the name to carry a size two characters long.

The figures share one column, so they can be read down. That is the thing running text cannot do at any length.

THIS HALF IS ALREADY BUILT

waDrawOrderReceipt already draws this table, waSendDocImage already uploads and sends it, and a text twin already goes instead when anything misses.

What is missing is the road: only the ASSISTANT can reach it today, and only with quantities in hand. The matcher's own answers still leave as plain text.

THE ONE THING TO DECIDE

The picture is not the message.

It arrives legible but small, and tapping opens it full size. That is not why the words matter: a picture cannot be copied, cannot be found by searching the chat, and costs data to fetch.

So the caption carries every price in words and the picture carries the layout. Neither alone is the answer -- and the words are the half that must survive if the image never loads.

ONE DEFECT FOUND IN THE DOCUMENT ITSELF

The drawn receipt's FAINT grey (#9CA3AF) is 2.54:1 on white, and it sets the column heads, the block heads and the footer line -- all at 11px, where the house floor is 4.5:1.

This is not new here; it is in waDrawOrderReceipt today, on the document a customer reads on a phone in the sun. That is the same reading condition that got the oxide chosen over amber in the first place.

Everything that carried FAINT now carries MUTE (#6B7280, 4.83:1). Nothing else about the document moves.
